docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Every InoFruits release for Minecraft 1.20.1, newest first, as published on CurseForge.

Released 2026-09-25 · Download

Six new Devil Fruits, eleven new abilities for existing fruits, and a balance pass. The addon goes from twenty-eight fruits to thirty-four, including its first Mythical Zoan.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.6.0 or newer.

⚠️ Update AkumaLib to 2.6.0 first. With an older AkumaLib the game refuses to start and says which version it needs. Existing worlds and servers need nothing else.

New fruits Zoan Uma Uma no Mi, Model: Unicorn: the unicorn

Mythical Zoan · golden box · 13 abilities

A Mythical Zoan on par with the base mod's Phoenix, and a healer as much as a fighter. The unicorn flies in both forms, leaving a rainbow behind it, and a crewmate can ride on its back.

The horn is the whole kit. Horn Thrust and Prism Lance go through armour, absorption and even a Logia's intangibility. Unicorn Charge runs through a line of enemies, Starfall calls five lances of light down on a spot, and Guiding Light draws a target to the user, an enemy to hit or a crewmate out of danger. On the other side, Purify and Sanctuary wash harmful effects away and keep new ones off the user and their allies. Moonlight Burst does both at once: the unicorn rears up, blasts enemies away and heals everyone on its side.

The Alicorn passive holds the horn's light: it burns away harmful effects as they land (hard control excepted) and heals the user while transformed. Horn blows refill it.

Kuma Kuma no Mi, Model: Grizzly: the grizzly bear

Zoan · iron box · 8 abilities

A brawler. A hybrid with huge clawed arms, or a whole grizzly on four legs. Claw Swipe knocks away everything in front, Salmon Swipe flips one target into the air, Maul charges and pins the first enemy it meets to the ground, and Roar slows and weakens everyone nearby while mobs run.

Two passives while transformed: Fury hits harder the more the bear is hurt (a gauge shows the bonus), and Thick Fur softens melee blows, resists knockback and keeps the cold out.

Paramecia Chi Chi no Mi: blood

Paramecia · golden box · 9 abilities

The user pays with their own blood and takes it back from others. Every technique costs blood. The Blood Reserve gauge fills with the blood the user loses and pays before their health does. A cost never kills.

Blood Spear, Blood Rush and Blood Pool make enemies bleed. Blood Tether pulls a bleeding enemy in (or drags a crewmate out of danger), and Blood Drain takes the blood back from everyone bleeding nearby to heal the user. Blood Shell clots into a thick shell that shatters on the enemies around it if it breaks. Blood Bond takes half the damage the crew suffers. And once the gauge is half full, Blood Festival spends all of it in a burst of spikes that hits harder the lower the user's health.

Oki Oki no Mi: law

Paramecia · golden box · 16 abilities

The user declares a law, and everyone around obeys it, the user included. Sixteen laws, one in force at a time, proclaimed in the chat of the players nearby: Halt, Grounded, Levitate, Truce, Ceasefire, Silence (no Devil Fruit powers), No Healing, No Escape, Disarm, No Haki, Reveal, Retribution (every blow comes back to its giver), Inversion (every heal hurts), Blindness, No Building and Walk.

The zone follows the user. Its size can be changed in the settings (32 blocks by default). The fruit wins by choosing the rule that hurts the other side more than it hurts you.

Kugi Kugi no Mi: nails

Paramecia · wooden box · 6 abilities

Nails that pin rather than kill. Kugizuke throws a big nail that roots the target, Kugibari fans small nails (three of them pin), and Kugi Ame rains nails on a spot. Kugi Yoroi makes nails stand out of the user's whole body, hurting whoever strikes or touches them. Kugi Dome nails the user's own feet down to hold their ground. Kuginuki rips every nail out of every body nearby, and the more nails, the more it hurts.

Kutsu Kutsu no Mi: shoes

Paramecia · wooden box · 7 abilities

Six pairs of soles, one worn at a time, drawn on the user's feet. Water Soles walk on water and lava, Wall Soles climb walls and hang from ceilings, Silent Soles make no sound and keep mobs from noticing, Weighted Soles cancel knockback, Spring Soles jump about seven blocks high with no fall damage, and Skate Soles glide fast on any ground. Stomp throws up everyone around, and hits harder in Weighted Soles.

New abilities for existing fruits
  • Kaze Kaze no Mi: Kyuin. The air reverses in front of the user and drags every enemy in a wide cone towards them.
  • Shio Shio no Mi: Shio Bashira. A pillar of salt that holds the target in place for 3 seconds and stops it healing for 10.
  • Shio Shio no Mi: Dassui. Draws the water out of every enemy around the user: they are hurt, slowed, salted and pulled slightly closer.
  • Tsuchi Tsuchi no Mi: Ryusa. Quicksand where the user looks, dragging enemies to its centre and wearing them down.
  • Tsuchi Tsuchi no Mi: Jisuberi. A landslide in front of the user that hurts, knocks away and briefly buries every enemy in a wide cone. Both new Tsuchi abilities have a bigger version, Dai-Ryusa and Dai-Jisuberi, while the earth golem is up.
  • Gamu Gamu no Mi: Hanekaeshi. A sheet of gum in the air that bounces every projectile back at whoever threw it.
  • Kane Kane no Mi: Zeni Nage. Flicks a golden coin at the target for 1 berry a throw. The luckier the user, the harder it hits.
  • Kane Kane no Mi: Oatari. For 30 seconds, creatures the user kills drop more loot and the ores they mine drop twice.
  • Kiza Kiza no Mi: Kiza Maki. Puts a slider on every enemy in a wide cone at once.
  • Kiza Kiza no Mi: Zen Hikisage. Pulls every slider around down at once: marked bodies lose both speed and strength, and the user takes a share of each.
  • Kiza Kiza no Mi: Oshiage. The user lowers their own slider to raise a marked ally's: they lose speed or strength, and the ally gains it.
Balance
  • Kaze Kaze no Mi hits harder. Oroshi, Kamaitachi and Tatsumaki deal more damage (Oroshi and Kamaitachi about 60% more).
  • Shio Shio no Mi hits harder. Kessho no Yari, Shio Barai and Shio no Ame deal about 50% more, and Shio no Wa hurts the undead more.
  • Tsuchi Tsuchi no Mi hits harder. Jibashiri and Tsubute deal more damage, in and out of the golem.
  • Mushi Mushi no Mi: Kyuketsu bites harder and stores a fixed amount of blood per bite.
  • Zuku Zuku no Mi: Kazakiribane's feathers deal twice as much damage. Washizukami carries its target for 8 seconds instead of 15.
  • Gamu Gamu no Mi: Fuusen's bubble bursts harder.
  • Mitsu Mitsu no Mi: Mitsu Suberi and Mitsu Numa deal twice as much damage. Mitsu Goromo is shorter (6 seconds instead of 8), slows less and has a longer cooldown.
Fixes
  • Kyuketsu and Nejikiri could hit a crewmate standing in front of the user instead of the enemy behind. Single-target attacks now only pick enemies.

Released 2026-09-25 · Download

A crash fix and redrawn fruit icons. No fruit, ability or balance changes. Existing worlds and servers need nothing special.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.4.0 or newer, the same as 3.0.0.

Fixes
  • The Kero Kero no Mi's tongue crashed the game. Tobitsuki crashed as soon as the tongue hit a block or a creature, and Shita as soon as it caught a creature. Both now work as described: Tobitsuki sticks to a block or a body and pulls the frog to it, and Shita catches its target.
Changes
  • All 28 fruit icons have been redrawn. Each fruit keeps its shape and colours, with a brighter look and a green stem like the base mod's fruits, so they sit better next to them in your inventory.

Released 2026-09-18 · Download

Thirteen new Devil Fruits and 80 new abilities. The addon goes from fifteen fruits to twenty-eight, and from 77 abilities to 157.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.4.0.

⚠️ AkumaLib 2.4.0 is required, not optional. 2.1.0 to 2.3.0 lack the classes this release uses (pulls, rendered lines, block protection), and the game crashes the first time one of them is needed. On a server, the server and every client must run the same AkumaLib: its network protocol changed, and mismatched versions refuse to connect.

⚠️ Three fruits from 2.0.0 were renamed, and some abilities need the fruit eaten again. Read Breaking changes, below the new fruits, before updating a world.

New fruits Logia Kaze Kaze no Mi — wind

Tier 3 · golden box · 9 abilities

The addon's largest kit, and a Logia built around moving people before hurting them. Toppu blows everything in front away, Josho lifts whatever stands in a column of rising air up to eighteen blocks, and the next two presses make it pay: Oroshi slams everything airborne within twelve blocks back into the ground, and Shippu turns the user into wind that rushes through a line of enemies.

Around that: Kamaitachi, a spinning disc of air that flies dead straight; Fuuheki, a wall of wind that deflects every projectile coming within four blocks; and Tatsumaki, a tornado that follows wherever the user looks. Rain does not stop it. Water still does. The user flies, faster outside of combat.

Paramecia Suji Suji no Mi — muscle

Tier 2 · iron box · 5 abilities

Three forms, each growing muscle somewhere different. The upper body hits extremely hard and very slowly, the legs run faster and jump higher without hitting any harder, and the full body does a bit of both, less well than either. Hasai punches out a shockwave that goes through enemies and walls; Choyaku jumps a long way and lands on whatever is underneath.

Mitsu Mitsu no Mi — honey

Tier 2 · iron box · 6 abilities

Almost no damage in the whole kit, and that is the design. Everything here decides where a fight happens: a pool of honey that slows anything standing in it (the user included), a coat that slows a target's movement and attacks, and Kohaku, honey that hardens into amber and locks a body in place for three seconds. Amahada coats the user so that anyone hitting them gets stuck, Mitsu Gusuri heals over time, and Mitsu Suberi slides on honey, leaving a sticky trail behind.

Gamu Gamu no Mi — chewing gum

Tier 2 · iron box · 5 abilities

A control kit with four verbs: root, shove, float, pull. Neba Dan sticks a target in place, Fuusen blows a bubble that drifts and pops on contact, Kikyu inflates a balloon that lets the user float down from any height, and Banji Gamu shoots a strand of gum up to thirty blocks and reels in whatever it catches, drawn as a real stretching strand. The passive glues the user's feet to walls and ceilings.

Neji Neji no Mi — twist

Tier 1 · wooden box · 5 abilities

Both forearms become spinning drills. Its signature is penetration: Rasen is the only technique in the addon that does not stop at the first body in its path, and drills a line through everything in front of the user. Nejikiri wrings one target off its feet, Totsushin charges drills first through a crowd, and Nejikomi tunnels through the ground and leaves the hole behind. It respects protected areas, like the base mod's own Mogu Mogu no Mi.

The drill arms are grafted onto the player's own body, so the hitbox does not change.

Wata Wata no Mi — cotton

Tier 1 · wooden box · 5 abilities

Cotton armour over the chest, shoulders and arms that softens hits and falls, a cloud that blinds anyone inside it and hides the user, and a packed ball of cotton that picks up whatever it hits and carries it off. Watazumi turns some of the user's cotton into white wool.

⚠️ The fruit has a drawback you cannot switch off: while the cotton armour is on, the user takes more damage from fire.

Kiza Kiza no Mi — the gauge

Tier 1 · wooden box · 3 abilities

No damage anywhere, and nothing created. Kiza Dashi puts a slider on a target, Hikisage pulls that slider down and hands the user whatever it took off, and Kiza Modoshi pulls back the user's own sliders, clearing every bad effect on them at once. Alone, the fruit can do nothing but cleanse. In front of one opponent, everything it takes, the user gains.

Kane Kane no Mi — treasure

Tier 1 · wooden box · 4 abilities

A fruit with no combat line at all, on purpose. Komyaku highlights everything valuable within thirty-two blocks, through walls. Meate marks the single most valuable thing within sixty-four blocks for two minutes. Nakami shows what is inside a container without opening it. And the passive keeps the user lucky: Devil Fruit boxes they open upgrade three times as often.

Zoan Mushi Mushi no Mi, Model: Mosquito

Tier 2 · iron box · 8 abilities

The addon's first form that is allowed to be bad at everything. The mosquito is weaker than a plain player on every line of the stat screen, and what pays for it is not on that screen: the smallest hitbox in the addon, and hostile mobs that do not bother targeting it. Both forms fly.

Kyuketsu drinks from whatever is in front of the user and heals them, and keeps part of that blood in a sac shown as a gauge. The blood slowly goes bad, and Chibukure spends all of it at once for a heal and a burst of speed. Kabashira raises a column of mosquitoes around the user that bites everything inside: the fruit's only answer to more than one opponent.

Kero Kero no Mi, Model: Frog

Tier 2 · iron box · 7 abilities

Light, vertical and immune to fall damage: the opposite of the crocodile it shares the water with. Its tongue does three things: Shita pulls a target in and holds it, Shita Muchi whips without pulling, and Tobitsuki sticks to a block or a body and pulls the frog to it. Hoppu jumps and slams whatever is underneath. Nendeki makes the skin sticky, and the next projectile of any kind that hits the user sticks harmlessly instead.

Fugu Fugu no Mi, Model: Pufferfish

Tier 1 · wooden box · 7 abilities

A defensive Zoan whose full form is too round for most doors. Bocho puffs the user into a spiky ball that shoves everything nearby away, Togeuchi fires a ring of spines in every direction, and Hosui blows a jet of air that throws the user backwards, out of trouble.

Two passives do the real work while a form is on: melee attackers take part of the blow back, and poison goes both ways, onto anyone the user hits and anyone who hits them.

Usa Usa no Mi, Model: Hare

Tier 1 · wooden box · 5 abilities

The addon's only evasion kit. The hare outruns anything on the ground and jumps far higher than a player, and Ushiro Geri, a two-legged kick that launches the target one way and the hare the other, is the hardest single hit in the wooden tier. It pays for all of it by being fragile: its two forms carry the lowest armour in the addon.

Kani Kani no Mi, Model: Crab

Tier 1 · wooden box · 4 abilities

A crab that breathes underwater and walks on the sea floor in its full form, and grows a shell and two pincers in its hybrid, where it is slow and hard to push around. Yokobashiri is a dash with no wind-up (sideways, in the shell), and Hasamikomi catches whatever is in front of the user in a claw and drags it along.

⚠️ Breaking changes — read before updating a world Three fruits and their forms have new ids

Six fruits were renamed during this cycle so that every root is two morae, the way the base mod names its own. Only three of them existed in 2.0.0, so only these three affect an existing world:

2.0.0 3.0.0 Itachi Itachi no Mi, Model: Ferret Ita Ita no Mi, Model: Ferret Fukuro Fukuro no Mi, Model: Owl Zuku Zuku no Mi, Model: Owl Kujira Kujira no Mi, Model: Whale Isa Isa no Mi, Model: Whale

Their ids changed with their names, along with the forms and abilities that carried the old root:

Kind 2.0.0 id 3.0.0 id Fruit inofruits:itachi_itachi_no_mi_model_ferret inofruits:ita_ita_no_mi_model_ferret Fruit inofruits:fukuro_fukuro_no_mi_model_owl inofruits:zuku_zuku_no_mi_model_owl Fruit inofruits:kujira_kujira_no_mi_model_whale inofruits:isa_isa_no_mi_model_whale Ability ferret_walk_point ita_ita_walk_point Ability ferret_heavy_point ita_ita_heavy_point Ability fukuro_fukuro_fly_point zuku_zuku_fly_point Ability fukuro_fukuro_assault_point zuku_zuku_assault_point Ability fukuro_fukuro_flight zuku_zuku_flight Ability kujira_kujira_walk_point isa_isa_guard_point — also renamed, see below Ability kujira_kujira_heavy_point isa_isa_heavy_point Ability kujira_rideable isa_rideable Morph ferret_walk, ferret_heavy ita_ita_walk, ita_ita_heavy Morph fukuro_fukuro_fly, fukuro_fukuro_assault zuku_zuku_fly, zuku_zuku_assault Morph kujira_kujira_walk, kujira_kujira_heavy isa_isa_guard, isa_isa_heavy

Ferret Dart keeps its id. The ferret's two forms now read Ita Ita Walk Point and Ita Ita Heavy Point, like every other Zoan in the addon.

The whale's full form is now a Guard Point. The base mod calls a defensive Zoan's full form a Guard Point (Zou, Mammoth, Brachiosaurus, Kame), and the whale is the addon's tank. The form is the same; only its name and id changed.

What carries over

The addon maps every old id to its new one when an older world loads, so:

  • fruits already in chests, inventories and item frames become the renamed fruits;
  • the forms and their effects resolve under their new ids.

Tested on a world created with 2.0.0: fruits in storage and players who had already eaten the ferret, owl or whale come through the update with their fruit and forms under the new names. If a form or an ability is still missing for someone, run /ability reset <player> and have them eat the fruit again.

Abilities added to fruits that were already out

Mine Mine no Mi grants a fruit's abilities when the fruit is eaten and never checks the fruit again. A player who already has one of these fruits will not see the new abilities until they run /ability reset <player> and eat the fruit again:

Fruit New in 3.0.0 Isa Isa no Mi (whale) Shiofuki, Utagoe Wani Wani no Mi Lunging Bite, Belly Crawl Nezu Nezu no Mi Hassho Chiku Chiku no Mi Chikuken Bai Bai no Mi Baizo The loot files are gone

The addon no longer ships loot_modifiers or loot_tables/dfboxes files. Its fruits are now added straight into Mine Mine no Mi's own Devil Fruit box pool, at the same weight as the base mod's fruits of the same tier. A datapack that overrode inofruits:loot_modifiers/* or inofruits:dfboxes/*_additions no longer does anything. To tune the rates, edit the base mod's box tables instead.

Changes to existing fruits New abilities
  • Wani Wani no Mi — Lunging Bite and Belly Crawl. Death Roll sat behind the crocodile's slowest form with no way to get in range. Lunging Bite throws the whole body a few blocks forward and ends on the first enemy in the way, further and harder in the full form. Belly Crawl slides the user in low and fast, and the next bite that lands hits harder. Death Roll also gets its own sound.
  • Isa Isa no Mi — Shiofuki and Utagoe. The whale finally has something to do while crowded: Shiofuki erupts a column of water in front of it that launches enemies into the air and puts out fires on everyone caught in it. Utagoe is a song that makes the user and nearby allies resist damage. Both reach further in the full form.
  • Nezu Nezu no Mi — Hassho. The rat's plague used to be something to watch spread. Hassho sets off every plague on nearby carriers at once, each taking all the damage its plague had left.
  • Chiku Chiku no Mi — Chikuken. A third way to spend the battery: the next punch carries all the stored force into one target. The most dangerous way to carry a charge, and the kit's highest single hit.
  • Bai Bai no Mi — Baizo. Every clone next to the user splits again, up to a limit. The Bai Bai no Mi is complete at three abilities.
Look and feel
  • Animations across every fruit, on the techniques where a pose helps, and the Zoans' full forms move with them: the crocodile rolls around its own spine, the crab's pincer snaps, the pufferfish holds its puff, the whale lands with a splat.
  • The Wani Wani no Mi's Heavy Point has a new model. The crocodile head replaces the player's, and the player's own body stays visible under osteoderms, a tail and claws. Its hitbox is smaller to match.
  • Sounds where they were missing: Bone Throw, Weasel Bound, Washizukami, and a generated wind for Tatsumaki and insect hum for Kabashira. Saigoppe's spray is replaced by a softer puff.
  • The Tsuri Tsuri no Mi's fishing line is drawn as a real line instead of a trail of particles.
  • The Kobo Kobo no Mi shows what it hits. Two of its techniques reach eight blocks and used to show nothing at all; they now leave particles, so the player can see what they hit.
  • New fruit sprites for the ferret, the owl, the whale and the Tsuchi Tsuchi no Mi, and ability icons redrawn without the dark outline the base mod's icons do not have.
  • Every ability description is rewritten to read like the base mod's: one short sentence saying what the technique does.
Fixes
  • Kajiru could gnaw open chests. The rat's bite only checked for claimed areas, so in the wild it could eat a chest, barrel, furnace, spawner or redstone component and spill its contents. It now follows the base mod's own block-protection list, which only allows terrain, building blocks, foliage and ore.
  • Hako Kobo emptied containers with griefing turned off. Spilling a container now counts as griefing, and respects the ability-griefing config and, for a mob caster, the mobGriefing rule.
  • Kabe's wall ignored the base mod's placement rules. It now goes through them like the base mod's own barriers do: griefing settings, challenge arena bounds, restricted blocks and restoring areas.
  • Ichi Ichi and Tsuri Tsuri ignored the protection whitelist at the target. A technique the server whitelisted was allowed where the caster stood and refused where the target stood.
  • Marks and side effects landed on hits that did nothing, such as a strike on an intangible Logia or an invulnerable body, and vanished on hits that did land whenever someone else had struck the same target a moment earlier. Both are fixed across the addon.
  • In randomized fruits mode, this addon's fruits showed their real icon under a "Generic Fruit" label, which gave them away. They are now disguised like every other fruit.
Under the hood

More of what this addon used to carry itself now comes from AkumaLib: pulling a body toward the user, lines drawn between two points, protected-area checks, and the way a Devil Fruit box picks up this addon's fruits. None of it is visible in game; all of it is why AkumaLib 2.4.0 is required.

How they fit into Mine Mine no Mi
  • They drop from its own Devil Fruit boxes, wooden, iron and golden, now as entries in the box's own pool at the same weight as the base mod's fruits of the same tier. Finding one is exactly as rare as finding any other fruit of its tier.
  • Both 2.0.0 limitations are gone. This addon's fruits now come out of the 5% tier cascade like the base mod's, and no box is held under its intended chance any more.
  • They appear in its Devil Fruits creative tab, and take part in randomized fruits mode.
  • They are calibrated against its kits, not above them.
  • The encyclopaedia, fruit shifting and "eat a fruit you already have" all pick them up unchanged.

Released 2026-09-10 · Download

Nine new Devil Fruits and 45 new abilities. The addon goes from six fruits to fifteen, and from 32 abilities to 77.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.1.0.

⚠️ AkumaLib 2.1.0 is required, not optional. 2.0.0 does not contain what this release compiles against, and loading against it fails during registration rather than gracefully.

New fruits Logia Tsuchi Tsuchi no Mi — earth

Tier 3 · golden box · 7 abilities

The first Logia whose element is everywhere, and its balance is a data file rather than a number. Every other Logia's Travel is bounded by its substance being rare — sand, ice, glass — so the earth tag deliberately stops at the dirt family: the user phases through the top layer of the world and stops the moment they go below it or step into a building. Stone is a wall, and that is the fruit's counter-play.

A wave along the ground, a temporary wall that takes itself back down, an immobilisation that does no harm at all and is the strongest thing in the kit, and one thrown mass. Over all of it, a golem form that grows every technique it holds — including their range, which is the axis such forms usually forget.

Yuge Yuge no Mi — steam

Tier 2 · iron box · 7 abilities

The only fruit in the game that carries water — the universal Devil Fruit weakness — to somebody standing on dry land. A soaked target loses their own fruit's powers for a moment, and every technique here is priced twice: once against a dry body, once against one the fruit has already soaked. It is the addon's first kit that always wants two presses.

Scalding damage doubles on a soaked body; the finisher is worth five times as much and uses the mark up. Around that: a lunge that soaks what it passes through, and a vent that lifts the user ten blocks and holds them there while the column below scalds whatever stays in it.

Its Logia body is immune to fire but not to lava, and takes half again as much from cold — the trade that pays for the immunity.

Paramecia Bai Bai no Mi — multiplication

Tier 3 · golden box · 2 abilities

The smallest kit in the addon, and deliberately so. What sets its tier is not damage: it can make a permanent copy of an item, which is worth more to a world than any number in this mod. Devil Fruits and containers holding other items are refused in code. The other ability puts three copies of the user on the field.

Both cooldowns are in the config file — this is the fruit a server owner is most likely to have an opinion about.

Ichi Ichi no Mi — swapping

Tier 2 · iron box · 5 abilities

Three techniques and a passive, no damage anywhere, and one idea under all of them: two places trade what is standing in them. Swap with any body still in sight, swap everything in a column twenty blocks across at once — the user included, with no say in where they land — or swap two other things and never move at all.

It is the addon's most lethal fruit without dealing a point of damage, and that is the intent: where somebody ends up is the weapon.

Chiku Chiku no Mi — accumulation

Tier 1 · wooden box · 3 abilities

A battery. It stores the force of every blow the user takes and gives the whole of it back at once — either at one target or at everything within six blocks. The shape comes from the base mod's own Karma, and the divergence is the point: this one only charges on a blow that actually lands.

Tsuri Tsuri no Mi — fishing

Tier 1 · wooden box · 4 abilities

The addon's first fruit that pulls. Everything that displaced anything before this pushed. All four abilities are one line read differently: take a body and bring it here, take a wall and bring the user to it, or bring back every dropped item and scrap of experience within twenty-six blocks.

Zoan Fukuro Fukuro no Mi, Model: Owl

Tier 2 · iron box · 7 abilities

The addon's first fruit that flies. Two forms that genuinely disagree: the owl is fast in the air, hopeless on foot and weightless in a fall; the hybrid hits twice as hard, flies slower and lands like a person. Silent flight, night vision, a grab that carries its target off, a wing beat that clears a room, and a thrown flight feather.

Nezu Nezu no Mi, Model: Rat

Tier 1 · wooden box · 5 abilities

The base mod has no small mammal at all — its smallest Zoan is the axolotl. The ferret beats this fruit on nearly every attribute and the Mogu Mogu keeps digging, so what is left for the rat is the thing neither of them has: a bite that spreads. Nothing else in the base mod or this addon carries an affliction from one body to another on its own.

Kujira Kujira no Mi, Model: Whale

Tier 1 · wooden box · 4 abilities

The addon's first tank, and the first Zoan here whose two forms are a real trade-off rather than a big one and a small one. The Walk Point stops playing and starts absorbing — the heaviest defence in the addon, on a body whose land speed is cut by 90% — while the Heavy Point keeps ordinary mobility and reach. One charge, which reads the form it is used in.

Changes to existing fruits
  • Death Sleep, a recovery hold for the ferret: it drops limp and does not get up. Nothing stops attacking it — it simply takes less, and mends fast while it lies there.
  • The Nezu Nezu no Mi moved to tier 1 during development, which took the iron box back off its chance ceiling. The Yuge Yuge no Mi has since put it back.
  • A new fruit sprite for the Fukuro Fukuro no Mi.
  • Status icons for the five effects that had none — they were drawing the missing-texture square in the HUD.
Fixes
  • Weasel Bound and Tail Sweep damaged their own caster. Both used a sphere that does not exclude the user.
  • Habataki's animation never stopped. The two-argument animation call runs until something calls stop, and a one-shot technique has nothing to call it from — so the wing-beat pose stayed on forever.
  • The paint blob never despawned when it hit a block, and went on flying.
  • The owl's Assault Point drew armour on arms that are wings.
  • canMount() was read backwards on the ferret and the crocodile. It means "may climb onto a vehicle", not "may be ridden" — the two forms could not sit in a boat or on a horse for no reason.
Under the hood

Most of the release's non-fruit work was moving this addon onto AkumaLib rather than keeping its own copies: eleven form gates, ten morph stat blocks, five effects, the targeting helpers and the amplified-presentation plumbing all now come from the library. None of it is visible in game; all of it is why 2.1.0 of the library is required.

How they fit into Mine Mine no Mi

Unchanged from 1.0.0, and worth repeating:

  • They drop from its own Devil Fruit boxes — wooden, iron and golden — so finding one is as rare as finding any other fruit of its tier.
  • They appear in its Devil Fruits creative tab, rather than in a tab of their own.
  • They are calibrated against its kits, not above them.
  • The encyclopaedia, fruit shifting and "eat a fruit you already have" all pick them up unchanged.
Known limitations
  • A fruit from this addon does not drop from the base mod's 5% tier cascade. That nested roll goes through a code path that skips loot modifiers by design, so only the direct box rolls can yield one.
  • The iron box is at its ceiling. With six tier 2 fruits, one roll cannot express the intended chance, so each of them shows up about 7% less often than its share. The wooden box is 20% under for the same reason. Both are deliberate: one chest yielding one fruit is worth more than the exact number.

Released 2026-09-07 · Download

The first release. Six Devil Fruits, 32 abilities, none of them in the base mod.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.0.0.

The fruits Shio Shio no Mi — salt

Logia · golden box · 7 abilities

A control Logia built on purification rather than dehydration. It denies more than it damages: a salted body stops regenerating and takes half of any other healing, a ring of salt sears the dead and strips weak blessings, and the user can come apart into a current of salt and pour through the air.

Hone Hone no Mi — bone

Paramecia · iron box · 6 abilities

Wear your own skeleton on the outside — and while it holds, every other technique in the kit hits harder. Throw a bone that curves back and strikes twice, grow a blade out of your arm, spray splinters, knit yourself back together.

Iro Iro no Mi — paint

Paramecia · wooden box · 5 abilities

Paid for in information and position, not damage. Sixteen colours, and the colour is a real choice: war paint gives a different bonus for each. Blind with a thrown blob, mark a target through walls, or take on the colours behind you — which holds only while you stand perfectly still.

Kobo Kobo no Mi — spill

Paramecia · wooden box · 4 abilities

Takes things away from people rather than taking them apart. Force a target to drop what it holds, empty every container nearby onto the floor at once, or leave everything around you starving.

Itachi Itachi no Mi, Model: Ferret

Zoan · iron box · 6 abilities

Mobility, not muscle. Three times a player's speed, a hitbox short enough to get where nobody else fits, and almost no armour to show for it. Two forms, a bounding leap, claws that leave a bleed, and a musk that leaves everything nearby reeling while the user walks away.

Wani Wani no Mi, Model: Crocodile

Zoan · iron box · 4 abilities

The ferret read backwards: an ambush predator. Slow and armoured on land, twice as fast in the water and able to breathe there. Its death roll takes hold in the jaws and rolls — beast form only, and deadlier in water — and a tail sweep throws everything around it clear.

How they fit into Mine Mine no Mi

Nothing here replaces or rebalances the base mod.

  • They drop from its own Devil Fruit boxes — wooden, iron and golden — so finding one is as rare as finding any other fruit of its tier.
  • They appear in its Devil Fruits creative tab, rather than in a tab of their own.
  • They are calibrated against its kits, not above them. The base mod's own numbers are the ceiling: a new fruit sits beside the Magu Magu and the Gomu Gomu in the same loot pool, so it has no business outclassing them.
  • The encyclopaedia, fruit shifting and "eat a fruit you already have" all pick them up unchanged.
Known limitations
  • A fruit from this addon does not drop from the base mod's 5% tier cascade. That nested roll goes through a code path that skips loot modifiers by design, so only the direct box rolls can yield one.
  • The crocodile's kit is the newest and the shortest; more abilities for it are planned.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Settings live in config/inofruits-common.toml:

Section Setting Default What it does bai_bai_no_mi fukuseiCooldown 6000 (5 min) Cooldown of Fukusei, which makes one permanent copy of the held item. The value that most affects a server's economy. bai_bai_no_mi baiBunshinCooldown 2400 (2 min) Cooldown of Bai Bunshin, which spawns three copies of the user for 30 seconds. bai_bai_no_mi baizoCooldown 1800 (90 s) Cooldown of Baizo, which doubles the clones already standing. bai_bai_no_mi baizoMaxClones 8 Most clones one player may have at once. A server performance limit. yuge_yuge_no_mi kumoriSuppression 60 (3 s) How long Kumori switches off a soaked Devil Fruit user's powers. 0 removes the suppression. oki_oki_no_mi okiRadius 32 blocks Radius of the Oki Oki no Mi's law zone around the user, from 8 to 64. Everyone inside obeys the law in force, the user included. Past about 48 blocks, players no longer see the creatures the law acts on.

Durations are in ticks (20 ticks = 1 second).

Ship the file to your players

The file is not synchronised to clients. The server always enforces its own values, but a player's ability tooltips read their copy. A server that changes a cooldown should give its players the same file, or their tooltips will show the defaults.

docs.title: Box odds
docs.text:
A Devil Fruit box gives one fruit at most. When it opens:

  • 5% of the time, it also rolls the next box up (wooden → iron → golden), and a fruit from there comes first;
  • 95% of the time, it rolls five fruits from its own list, where every fruit is equally likely;
  • it keeps the first fruit still available: with one fruit per world, a fruit someone already has is skipped.

With every fruit still available, no Luck and only Mine Mine no Mi and InoFruits installed:

Box Fruits in the box Each of its own fruits A fruit from a higher box No fruit Wooden 39 (15 from InoFruits) 2.32% iron 4.52%, golden 0.238% 4.76% Iron 40 (12 from InoFruits) 2.26% golden 4.75% 4.76% Golden 26 (7 from InoFruits) 3.65% — 5.00%

docs.title: What changes the odds
docs.text:
• Luck: each point of the Luck attribute adds 5% to the chance of rolling the next box up, and takes 5% off the chance of rolling fruits. The base mod's New World, once active, counts as one more point.
  • Fruits already found: with one fruit per world, a fruit someone already has is skipped and the box looks further down its five rolls, so the remaining fruits come up more often.
  • Other addons that add fruits to the boxes share the same odds: each new fruit makes every other one of its box a little rarer.

Figures computed from Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5's box logic and the boxes as the game loads them with InoFruits, then checked against 200,000 simulated openings of each box.

The box icons are the Devil Fruit box textures of Mine Mine no Mi, by Wynd and its other authors, shown to identify the boxes. The fruit sprites are InoFruits' own.

docs.title: Sky Island
docs.text:
Mine Mine no Mi: Sky Island adds Skypiea as a dimension of its own to Mine Mine no Mi: the sea of clouds, the Angel Islands and their Skypiean villages, and the Upper Yards where the City of Gold was lost. The way up is a Knock-Up Stream erupting from the floor of the deep ocean.

Version documented 0.2.0 (beta) Mod id inosky Download CurseForge · 0.2.0 · changelog

A beta

Worlds are generated from this version's rules. A later version may change what stands in chunks that have not been explored yet.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Mod Version Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge 47 or later Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 AkumaLib 2.6.1 or later

Client and server.

The base mod's sky islands

Mine Mine no Mi's own sky islands no longer generate in the overworld: Skypiea takes their place. Those already generated in an existing world stay where they are.

docs.title: The dimension
docs.text:
Getting there and back the Knock-Up Stream, the arrival, falling back to the overworld Angel Islands islands of cloud: Skypiean villages, the White Berets, Angel Beach, Heaven's Gate Upper Yards the great islands of earth: the Giant Jack, Shandora, the Shandias and their camps Wildlife the South Bird, two flying mounts, the Cloud Fox and the Giant Dog Configuration the geyser's rhythm, the fall back, the dials; the /geyser command

Skypiea sits above the overworld's deep oceans and nowhere else: its islands and its sea of clouds only exist where the overworld below is deep ocean. The cloud sea is a sea you swim in and sail on, with a swell; boats float on it.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• Worldgen mods: Skypiea reads the overworld's own biomes to find the deep oceans (minecraft:is_deep_ocean) and changes nothing in the overworld beyond the geyser.
  • Valkyrien Skies 2 (optional, 2.4.11 or later): a ship sailed into an erupting Knock-Up Stream rises to Skypiea with its crew, lands on open cloud sea and floats on it. A ship that falls out of Skypiea goes back to the overworld with its crew. Anybody seated at the helm arrives standing on the deck. Sky Island never requires Valkyrien Skies.

docs.title: Angel Islands
docs.text: Two islands in three are Angel Islands: low islands made of island cloud from top to bottom, a few trees rooted in the cloud. Their shore is a cliff down to a flat shelf at the level of the cloud sea — Angel Beach.

docs.title: Skypiean villages
docs.text:
Every Angel Island has a village of houses in cloud brick, cut cloud and shell tiles, with streets, a square, and Skypiean civilians and traders (the base mod's own). The larger islands have larger villages, with:

  • an inn;
  • a bandstand;
  • kitchen gardens on cloud farmland;
  • a cloud fountain.

docs.title: Cloud farmland
docs.text: A hoe tills island cloud into cloud farmland, and crops grow in it exactly as in farmland: water nearby keeps it moist, and trampled or left bare it turns back into island cloud.

docs.title: The village blocks
docs.text: Every block the villages are built from can be crafted: cloud brick, cut cloud, cloud pillars and walls, shell tiles, awning cloth, cloud glass, conch lanterns and Vearth urns. A recipe viewer (JEI or EMI) shows the recipes.

docs.title: The White Berets
docs.text: Skypiea's police. Every village has their post, with a rare chest of seized goods, and recruits and a captain who keep order in the village. They are calibrated against the base mod's own NPCs — the captain is the stronger, with Busoshoku Haki.

docs.title: Angel Beach
docs.text:
The flat shore at the foot of an Angel Island's cliffs.

  • Dials wash up on the beach over time, a few at a time, and are picked up like any item. How often, and how many a stretch of beach holds, is in the configuration.
  • A seafront, once per village island, facing the island's geyser: the dial workshop, a promenade along the shore, a pier, deck chairs, and sometimes a castle of cloud.
  • One to three White Beret lookouts along the shore, away from the seafront, each with its guard.

docs.title: Heaven's Gate
docs.text: The way into Skypiea, on every village island: the gate, its tunnel through the bank of cloud, and a causeway from the tunnel to the promenade. The geyser sets you down right in front of it.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Every Sky Island release for Minecraft 1.20.1, newest first, as published on CurseForge.

docs.title: 0.2.0 (beta)
docs.text:
Released 2026-09-26 · Download

Skypiea comes alive: its first animals. Giant South Birds that always face south, two birds you can tame, saddle and fly, the Cloud Fox and the huge Giant Dog as companions - the dog a mount too. And a round of fixes: every village island gets its Heaven's Gate, geysers keep their vent, and exploring Skypiea no longer floods the log.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.6.1 or newer (was 2.5.0). Client and server.

⚠️ Still a beta: worlds are generated from this version's rules. Chunks already explored keep what they have; islands you have not reached yet may get a Heaven's Gate they would not have had in 0.1.0 (see Fixes).

New: the birds of Skypiea
  • The giant South Bird (Upper Yards): the Jaya bird, grown huge on Skypiea and friendly. A living compass - once it stops, it turns to face south, beak and all.
  • The Sky Dot Bird (Pierre's kind) - pink and dotted, rare on the Angel Islands and in the Upper Yards - and the Three-Jo Bird (Fuza's kind) - a great lilac vulture, rarer still, in the Upper Yards only. Both are flying mounts:
    • tame them with seeds (like a parrot), then put a vanilla saddle on them;
    • only their owner rides and steers them;
    • fly like a horse that flies: the movement keys go the way you look, Jump climbs, Sneak descends, with neither they hover;
    • in the air, Sneak never drops you off - land first, then Sneak to get down;
    • fall out of Skypiea on one and you both go home, still in the saddle.
  • Their wings fold on the ground, beat fast when hovering or climbing, slow when cruising, and hold still in a dive; they bank into turns - with a rider too.
  • Drops: feathers and meat (cooked if they burned), more with Looting; a mount's saddle drops too.
New: companions
  • The Cloud Fox (Su's kind), on the Angel Islands: tame it with fish. It follows you, and lies down on the cloud when told to sit.
  • The Giant Dog (Holy's kind), very rare in the Upper Yards, huge: tame it with raw meat.
    • A guard, like a wolf: it goes for whatever strikes you and whatever you strike (never creepers, ghasts or your other animals), and catches up with you when it gets stuck in the trees.
    • A mount: saddle it and ride it like a horse - Jump leaps about three blocks. No fall damage under ten blocks.
    • 80 health, 8 attack damage.
  • Five coats each, the first the manga's own: fox cloud, sky, dawn, mint, dusk; dog cream, russet, silver, chocolate, charcoal.
Fixes
  • Geysers keep their vent: an amethyst geode next to a geyser could crush it. A geyser now repairs its crater by itself.
  • Heaven's Gate on every village island: about half of them had none. Where the gate needs the room, the beach's deck chairs, castle or workshop are left out.
  • You always arrive in front of the gate, never on its roof, even on a sloping coast.
  • Valkyrien Skies: a ship arriving by geyser no longer lands on Heaven's Gate; it looks further out for open cloud sea where the sea is shallow.
  • Exploring Skypiea is smoother: the game no longer fills its log with warnings each time new land appears, which slowed it down. The islands themselves are unchanged.
Known issues
  • Some Angel Islands have no White Beret lookout, or one oddly placed.
  • The Shandias' hidden village sometimes sits partly on an island instead of on the sea.
  • Some small Upper Yards have a single Shandia camp.
  • In a few worlds, leaves block the Giant Jack's ramp.

docs.title: 0.1.0 (beta)
docs.text:
Released 2026-09-24 · Download

The first release. A Forge addon for Mine Mine no Mi that adds Skypiea as a dedicated dimension, reached by riding a Knock-Up Stream up from the floor of the deep oceans: the cloud sea, the Angel Islands and their Skypiean villages, the beach, Heaven's Gate, and the Upper Yards with the Giant Jack, the ruins of Shandora and the Shandias.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.5.0 or newer. Client and server.

⚠️ The base mod's own sky islands no longer generate in the overworld: Skypiea replaces them. Structures already generated in an existing world stay where they are.

⚠️ A beta: worlds are generated from this version's rules. A later version may change where islands and structures stand in chunks not yet explored.

The way up: the Knock-Up Stream
  • A geyser on the floor of the deep oceans, one for each island above. Every ten minutes it rumbles for thirty seconds, then erupts for ninety (all configurable).
  • The column throws whatever is caught in it into the sky - players, mobs, dropped items, boats with their riders - and sends it on to Skypiea. An eruption always lasts long enough to carry somebody from the sea floor to the top.
  • You arrive on the ground or on the cloud sea, never inside a block: in front of Heaven's Gate on an island with a village.
  • /locate structure inosky:knock_up_stream finds one. /geyser tells where the nearest one is and when it erupts; /geyser now makes it erupt at once (operators).
The way down
  • Step off an island and sink through the cloud sea: below the bottom of Skypiea you come out high above the same place in the overworld, with slow falling. Boats come back too.
Skypiea
  • Islands only above the overworld's deep oceans; open cloud sea everywhere else above deep water, nothing above land.
  • The cloud sea: a sea of cloud you swim in, with a swell, bluish and animated so it is never mistaken for island cloud. Boats float and sail on it.
  • Its own sky, and no lava sea under it.
  • Island cloud, sea cloud and the Knock-Up Core are the dimension's own blocks; the Upper Yards are made of the overworld's earth and stone - the Vearth of the Blue Sea.
Angel Islands

Two islands in three: low islands of island cloud from top to bottom, a few trees rooted in the cloud. * Skypiean villages: houses of cloud brick, cut cloud and shell tiles, streets and a square, Skypiean civilians and traders (the base mod's own). Larger villages on the larger islands, with an inn, a bandstand, kitchen gardens and a cloud fountain. * Cloud farmland: a hoe tills island cloud, and crops grow in it exactly as in farmland. * The White Berets: their post in every village (with a rare chest of seized goods), recruits and a captain policing the village - calibrated against the base mod's NPCs. * The village blocks can be crafted: cloud brick, cut cloud, cloud pillars, shell tiles, awning cloth, cloud glass, conch lanterns, Vearth urns. * Angel Beach: the flat shore at the foot of the cliffs. Dials wash up on it over time. A seafront once per village island - the dial workshop, a promenade, a pier, deck chairs, sometimes a cloud castle - and one to three White Beret lookouts along the shore. * Heaven's Gate: the way into Skypiea on every village island - the gate, its tunnel, and a causeway to the promenade.

Upper Yards

One island in three, rarer and far larger: jungle plains around y 100, and massifs rising to about 215. * The Giant Jack (one Upper Yard in three): a beanstalk climbable to the top, a ramp up its whole height, and the Golden Bell at the summit with its chest - one or two boxes, a Golden Box in about two chests in five. * Shandora, the City of Gold (a little over half of the Upper Yards, sometimes beside a Giant Jack): its square, avenues and halls, the stepped temple and its altar, and the crypt under the Poneglyph - the treasure, one or two boxes a chest. Halls, altar and crypt all hold boxes now and then. * Small ruins of Shandora: one to three per Upper Yard in the jungle - an altar, a colonnade, a fallen house, a sacred well. * The Shandias: warriors and a chief guarding their land. They attack only looters - open their chests and they come for you. Their own weapons, the Shandia spear and the burn bazooka, and skills from dials (burn bazooka, impact, breath dash, sky step, the chief's reject). * Shandia war camps: two to four per Upper Yard, in clearings of the plains - four tipis round a fire, a totem, a weapon rack, a lookout. A chest in every tipi. * The hidden village: the Shandias' village in a pocket of cloud on the sea at the island's foot, opening on the sea - six tipis round a square, the statue of Kalgara, totems along the path, the chief by the fire.

Compatibility
  • Worldgen mods: Skypiea reads the overworld's own biomes to find the deep oceans (minecraft:is_deep_ocean) and changes nothing in the overworld beyond the geyser.
  • Valkyrien Skies 2 (optional, 2.4.11 or newer): a ship in an erupting Knock-Up Stream rises to Skypiea with its crew, lands on open cloud sea and floats on it; a ship that falls out of Skypiea goes back to the overworld with its crew. Sky Island never requires VS.
Configuration

<world>/serverconfig/inosky-server.toml: * geyser: cycle_ticks (12000), eruption_ticks (1800), charge_ticks (600); * return: return_y (-32), the height below which a body falls back to the overworld; * angel_beach: dial_chance (2000), dial_cap (2), how often dials wash up and how many a stretch of beach holds.

Known issues
  • An amethyst geode generated in a neighbouring chunk can crush a geyser's vent (#42).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Sky Island's settings are per world, in <world>/serverconfig/inosky-server.toml, created the first time the world is loaded with the mod. A save carries its own geyser rhythm.

Edit it with the world closed

Forge rewrites a world's server config when the world unloads: a change made while the game is running is lost. To see an eruption without waiting, use /geyser now instead.

docs.title: geyser
docs.text:
The Knock-Up Stream's rhythm. 20 ticks make a second.

Setting Default What it does cycle_ticks 12000 (10 minutes) Ticks between one eruption starting and the next. eruption_ticks 1800 (90 seconds) How long an eruption lasts. An eruption too short to carry somebody from the sea floor to the top is lengthened. charge_ticks 600 (30 seconds) The warning before an eruption: bubbles and rumbling.

docs.title: return
docs.text: Setting Default What it does return_y -32 Below this height in Skypiea, a body is given back to the overworld, above the same place. From -64 to 40.

docs.title: angel_beach
docs.text:
The dials the sea leaves on the shore of the Angel Islands.

Setting Default What it does dial_chance 2000 One random tick in this many, on a beach surface, lays a dial. 0 turns it off. dial_cap 2 The most dials a stretch of beach (8 blocks around) holds at once.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Permission What it does /geyser operator where the nearest geyser within 64 blocks is, what it is doing and when it erupts /geyser now operator makes that geyser erupt at once

docs.title: The Knock-Up Stream
docs.text:
A Knock-Up Stream is a geyser on the floor of the deep ocean. There is one for every island in Skypiea, beside it below: a crater of dark prismarine and tuff round the Knock-Up Core.

/locate structure inosky:knock_up_stream

docs.title: An eruption
docs.text:
Phase Default What happens Quiet the rest of the cycle a bubble column marks the geyser Charge 30 seconds bubbles and rumbling: the warning Eruption 90 seconds the column rises to the sky

A cycle lasts ten minutes by default, and each geyser is offset in it by its own position: two geysers rarely erupt at the same moment. All three lengths are in the configuration.

The column lifts whatever is caught in it: players, mobs, dropped items, and boats with everyone aboard. At the top it sends them on to Skypiea. An eruption always lasts long enough to carry somebody from the sea floor to the top, whatever the configuration says.

docs.title: The arrival
docs.text: You come down on the ground or on the cloud sea, never inside a block. On an island with a village, the geyser sets you down in front of its Heaven's Gate; a boat arrives with its riders still in it.

docs.title: The way back
docs.text:
Step off an island and sink through the cloud sea. Below the bottom of Skypiea you come out high above the same place in the overworld, with slow falling long enough to land safely — over the sea, since Skypiea only lies above the deep oceans. Boats come back too.

The height of the fall back is return_y in the configuration.

docs.title: For operators
docs.text: Command What it does /geyser where the nearest geyser within 64 blocks is, what it is doing and when it erupts /geyser now makes that geyser erupt at once

docs.title: Upper Yards
docs.text: One island in three is an Upper Yard: rarer and far larger than an Angel Island, made of the Blue Sea's earth — the Vearth the Skypieans revere. Jungle plains around y 100, and massifs of rock rising to about 215.

docs.title: The Giant Jack
docs.text: One Upper Yard in three has the Giant Jack: a beanstalk that towers over the island from its highest massif, climbable all the way up by a ramp around it. At the top hangs the Golden Bell, with a chest beneath it — one or two boxes, a Golden Box in about two chests in five.

docs.title: Shandora, the City of Gold
docs.text:
A little over half of the Upper Yards hold the ruins of Shandora, sometimes beside a Giant Jack (never within reach of its stalk): a square, avenues, halls, a broken tower, the stepped temple with its altar, and under the square the crypt beneath the Poneglyph.

Where What it may hold The halls gold, common dials, extols; a box in about two chests in five The temple's altar gold, diamonds, emeralds, rare dials; a box in nine chests in ten The crypt the treasure: gold, diamonds, netherite, very rare items, a heavy extol pouch — one or two boxes a chest

Small ruins of Shandora lie in the jungle too, one to three per Upper Yard: a forgotten altar, a colonnade, a fallen house, a sacred well.

docs.title: The Shandias
docs.text:
The warriors of Shandora, and their chief, guarding their land. They attack only looters: leave their chests shut and they leave you alone.

  • Their weapons: the Shandia spear and the burn bazooka, both items of this mod.
  • Their skills, from dials: the burn bazooka, impact, a breath dash, a sky step, and the chief's reject.
  • Few of them at a time: a chief and a warrior on Shandora's square, one in the temple, one in the tower.

docs.title: Shandia camps
docs.text:
War camps: two to four per Upper Yard, in clearings of the plains, away from the city, the Giant Jack and the ruins. Four tipis round a fire, a totem, a weapon rack and a lookout, with two warriors.

The hidden village: the Shandias' own village, in a pocket of cloud on the sea at the island's foot, its only opening facing the sea. Six tipis round a square, the statue of Kalgara, totems along the path, and the chief by the fire.

There is a chest in every tipi: weapons, war dials, gold and emeralds, an extol pouch, food and arrows — and now and then a Wooden or an Iron Box.

docs.title: Wildlife
docs.text:
Skypiea's animals, after the manga: two birds you can ride, a living compass, and two companions. All of them come down on solid ground in the light, never on leaves; nothing spawns on the beach or the cloud sea, and no monster spawns anywhere in Skypiea.

Animal Where Tamed with What it is South Bird Upper Yards, commonest — a living compass Sky Dot Bird Angel Islands and Upper Yards, rare seeds a light flying mount Three-Jo Bird Upper Yards only, rarer seeds a great flying mount Cloud Fox Angel Islands fish a companion Giant Dog Upper Yards only, very rare raw meat a guard and a mount

All five have spawn eggs in the Skypiea creative tab.

docs.title: The South Bird
docs.text: The bird of Jaya, grown huge on Skypiea (about two blocks tall), and friendly. It perches and takes to the air now and then. A living compass: whenever it stops, it swings round to face south, beak and all — a way to find your bearings on a sea of clouds.

docs.title: The flying mounts
docs.text:
The Sky Dot Bird (Pierre's kind) is pink and dotted, quick and a strong climber. The Three-Jo Bird (Fuza's kind) is a great lilac vulture with a salmon ruff: bigger and tougher, slower to climb.

Sky Dot Bird Three-Jo Bird Health 30 50 Taming one seed in 5 one seed in 10 Wingspan about 4.5 blocks about 6.5 blocks
  1. Tame it with seeds (wheat, melon, pumpkin, beetroot or torchflower), like a parrot. Seeds also heal a tamed one.
  2. Saddle it: use a vanilla saddle on it. Without a saddle, a click makes it sit or stand.
  3. Ride it: use it with an empty hand. Only its owner can ride and steer it.

Flying it — a horse that flies:

Key In the air Movement keys fly the way you look Jump climb Sneak descend neither hover where you are

Getting off

In the air, Sneak descends and never drops you off. Land, then Sneak to get down. Holding Sneak all the way to the ground gets you off as soon as it touches down.

Below the cloud sea, the bird and its rider fall back to the overworld together, the rider still in the saddle. A mount takes no fall damage.

docs.title: The Cloud Fox
docs.text: Su's kind: a small white fox with a long muzzle, on the Angel Islands. Tame it with fish (raw cod or salmon); it follows you, and lies down on the cloud when you click it. It never fights. 12 health.

docs.title: The Giant Dog
docs.text:
Holy's kind: a huge dog — over three blocks tall — very rare in the Upper Yards. Tame it with raw meat (beef, pork or mutton).

  • A guard, like a wolf: it goes for whatever strikes you and whatever you strike — never creepers, ghasts or your other animals. It catches up with you by leaping to your side when it gets stuck in the trees.
  • A mount: put a vanilla saddle on it and ride it like a horse. The movement keys go the way you look; Jump leaps about three blocks. Ridden, it bites nothing of its own accord. Sneak + click still makes it sit or stand.
  • Tough: 80 health, 8 attack damage, hard to knock back, and no fall damage under ten blocks (half beyond).

docs.title: Coats
docs.text:
The fox and the dog are born in one of five coats and keep it for life; the first is the manga's own.

Coats Cloud Fox cloud (Su), sky, dawn, mint, dusk Giant Dog cream (Holy), russet, silver, chocolate, charcoal

docs.title: Drops
docs.text: The birds drop feathers and meat (cooked if they burned), more with Looting: one to three feathers and one or two pieces of meat from the South Bird and the Sky Dot Bird, two to five and two or three from the Three-Jo Bird. A saddled mount drops its saddle.
